Senses.Explanation: Outside phenomena there is no mind is one half of a reciprocal mind-and-phenomena formula that masters quote to deny an independently located mind or teaching-object. Yongming Yanshou uses it to block both permanence and annihilation: if phenomena stood outside mind one error would follow, while if mind stood outside phenomena another would. Jianxin Laifu states the reciprocal pair directly—this mind is phenomena, outside phenomena no mind; these phenomena are mind, outside mind no phenomena. Huangbo Xiyun gives the same formula and continues that mind itself is no-mind, warning that deliberately making mind mindless turns it into something existent. The phrase therefore frames direct teaching but does not license a new hidden substance called mind.
